recipes.name: Brioche
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon vegetable oil, or as needed

steps.text: Dissolve yeast in warm water in a small bowl. Let stand until creamy, about 10 minutes.

Stir together flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the center, then add eggs and yeast mixture; beat well until dough comes together. (Tip: Add 1 to 3 tablespoons of additional warm water, 1 tablespoon at a time, only if needed to help the dough come together.)
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and supple, about 8 minutes.
Flatten dough and spread it with 1/3 of the butter.
Repeat this step twice to incorporate remaining butter, allowing dough to rest for a few minutes between additions of butter, about 20 minutes total.
Lightly grease a large bowl with vegetable oil, place dough in the bowl, and turn to coat. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Punch down dough, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 6 hours to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease two 8x4-inch loaf pans.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide dough into 2 equal pieces, form into loaves, and place into the prepared loaf pans.
Cover with greased plastic wrap and let rise until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Make egg wash: Beat egg yolk and cold water in a small bowl. Brush on the tops of loaves.
Bake loaves in the preheated oven until the tops are deep golden brown, about 25 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Brioche
raw_recipe.description: This best brioche recipe yields a rich, buttery dough that can be shaped into rolls for a morning snack served with jam, or used in savory dishes.

review.reviewBody: may seem a little complicated but its not, its actually very easy to make. And my I add very delicious.

This recipe works perfectly. I used bread flour and refrigerated it overnight. In the morning the dough was firm and easy to work with. I made brioche a tete, and it yield 10 beautiful brioches. I added nuts and jam 'under the tetes' of a couple of them before baking, for myself - and the rest I kept plain for my family to add whatever they wanted to when eating.
They baked to perfection in 12 mins...In the future I plan to use this dough recipe for meat wrapping.

I used this recipe to make Hot Cross Buns for Easter. Followed the recipe to the end but with half the eggs and butter (which I subbed for margarine). I added candied peel, sultanas and cinnamon to the dough at the last stage and divided into buns. Let them prove for another 30 minutes and then baked them. They turned out great!
I made this into a king cake for Mardi Gras with great results: a bit of cinnamon sugar and some icing, delicious!

Like a couple of the other reviewers, I thought I'd done something wrong when I got to the butter addition. The dough broke apart and didn't incorporate the butter as easily as I wanted it to but I got it done. I have not baked this bread recipe as is, instead I used the dough to make cinnamon rolls. They were the best I've ever had! Thank you for sharing this recipe.

Made three batches, one was plain, one with choco chips and one with fruit jam as topping. All were perfect. Had little trouble with making exact brioche shape, so we made a little dent on top to fill in the toppings. Served it with home made lemon jelly, everybody loved it.

I didn't think it really tasted like brioche but it tasted really good! I have never made bread with this much butter - this uses as much as croissants. It felt lumpy and very greasy when I was kneading it. I followed the instructions exactly. The initial rise went well. But coming out of the refrigerator the next morning, it was completely impossible to divide it into loaves because the butter had solidified, so I had to let it warm up for several hours. Once I got it into loaves, it barely rose at all, even after 4 hours. I baked it anyway, in two loaves, and they turned out less than 3 inches high baked. Still, it tasted really good with a flaky, crunchy crust, something between soft bread and a biscuit (the best biscuits I have ever tasted). Next time, I will try just baking it as one loaf to see what happens. The crumb was very soft. As a side note, I used active dry yeast packets and European style butter (Kerrygold).

Love this recipe. Works great in a stand mixer. I had to add a little extra flour but it turned out great and it's easy to shape. I made knots out of this recipe and added garlic and herbs. Definitely a keeper.

This was an outstanding bread. It was soft and buttery, with a just-shy-of-firm crust. I substituted bread flour to get a firmer dough. I kneaded it with a stand mixer equipped with a dough hook, which took most of the work out of it, and also resulted in a nicely spongy, tight crumb.

This recipe is actually really simple. I made two loaves. The part that made me most iffy was kneading the soft butter into the dough. It was really slimy, and this being my first time making brioche, I worried that I was doing something wrong, but it came out fine! In fear of having plain bread as mentioned in other reviews, I added about 1/4 cup more of butter, and the bread is definitely delicious by itself. The bread is really soft on the inside with a slight crunchy exterior. I'll use it for French toast as well as eat it by itself or with butter. I'll make this again!
Absolute yummy perfection! I left the dough overnight in the fridge but it was so worth it to be able to bake a fresh loaf for breakfast.
This was my first time making bread, and I liked the texture. Next time, I'll make it with bread flour and some other ingredients.

It's a good recipe! While making the recipe, the entire kitchen smelled like a bakery! Even though the butter amount seems like a lot, and you must punch the dough a lot, it's worth the effort! The buttery bread is just eaten like this, perfect for breakfast! I accidentally added the yeast 1 hour later. Very easy to make, but just time consuming.
The manual kneading instructions were spot on. Just be prepared for a fair amount of work. My chocolate chunk brioche rolls had great flavor and a really nice feathery texture.
I made it to the recipe several times now and I put sesame seeds on the egg yolk.
This is soo good recipes. Thanks
I have never made brioche. This recipe was easy to follow. My bread turned out flaky and light. However, the flavor was a let down.
I followed the recipe exactly. No changing of ingredients, no changing the order of things. Lovely recipe and lovely bread.
Great recipe! I’m a relatively inexperienced bread maker and I feel like this first try at brioche was successful! Thank you for a simple recipe with good instructions and tips.
